correctness.rationale: For all projections deleting one coordinate, T projects bijectively, making every codimension-one facet restriction unique. Sections over the full simplex are T, but sections on its boundary are all q^n words; this obstructs flabbiness. The q^(n-1) top simplices each has its own free face deleting color n, giving a collapse to dimension n-2. K(T) shares the entire (n-2)-skeleton of the join of n discrete q-point sets, hence is (n-3)-connected; reduced Euler count is (-1)^(n-2)B. The graph case n=3 and Hurewicz/Whitehead for n>=4 give an actual sphere wedge rather than just Betti ranks. Independently checked Euler identities for n=3,4,5 and q=2,3 (e.g. B(3,2)=3 and B(4,2)=7). The source Python checker was read, not taken as an infinite proof.
